title: Model Adoption Micro-Segmentation & Channel Signal Atlas
creator: Lina Torres
description: Build a repeatable framework and artifact set that maps model adoption likelihood across granular buyer micro-segments and distribution channels. This initiative synthesizes telemetry, buyer interviews, synthetic workload probes, and public competitor signals into a prioritized atlas that informs provisioning, pricing, and go-to-market intervention decisions. Focus is on 'why' a model/variant wins in a segment (latency tolerance, quantization appetite, regulatory constraints, cost elasticity) and 'how' we detect early shifts in supply or demand that should trigger provisioning or sales outreach.
goals: Produce a 12-cell micro-segmentation matrix (by buyer archetype x channel) with adoption likelihood scores for top 20 model variants
Define 6 automated telemetry signals that map to adoption triggers (e.g., 95th pct latency spikes, token-cost sensitivity, model-fallback frequency)
Deliver an Atlas doc + 3 dashboards that allow sales/solutions teams to filter by vertical/region/latency-tolerance
Create a runbook that ties signal thresholds to operational actions (provision Dedicated capacity, enable quantized variant rollout, sales play activation)
deliverables: Signal definitions and instrumentation spec (CSV + schema)
Three Looker/Grafana dashboards: Segment Overview, Channel Signals, Variant Risk Monitor
Operational runbook mapping signals to provisioning and GTM actions
Experiment plan for validating signal thresholds using synthetic workload probes
approach: Phase 1: Desk research + competitor signal crawl (public changelogs, pricing updates, provider status feeds). Phase 2: Telemetry enrichment (add tags for channel, buyer cohort, model-variant). Phase 3: Field interviews (6-8 accounts across SMB, midmarket, enterprise) to validate segmentation assumptions. Phase 4: Synthetic probes to measure latency/cost sensitivity across representative payloads. Phase 5: Atlas synthesis, dashboard build, and runbook cadence. Emphasis on defensible scoring and low false-positive triggers for operational actions.

risks: Signal noise causing frequent false positives and unnecessary provisioning costs
Insufficient sample size in field interviews leading to mis-segmentation
Telemetry tagging rollout delayed by infra priorities
Competitor signal sources may be rate-limited or noisy
acceptance_criteria: Atlas includes scored adoption likelihood for >=20 model variants across 12 buyer-channel cells
At least 6 telemetry signals are instrumented and producing >=30 days of data in staging
Dashboards allow filtering by region, vertical, buyer-cohort, and model-variant
Runbook contains clear action thresholds and has sign-off from SRE and Sales Ops
